cues.en: I'm Bill Gurley. I got to Silicon Valley in about 1997 and was fortunate enough to become a venture capitalist in 98. And the entire, you know, first year of my career, I had zero interest in interacting with any form of government. It didn't seem necessary for what I was trying to do. I was working with founders and software and technology. I didn't see what it would bring me. Until one day where I ran into an issue, which I'll tell you about later, that required
cues.zh: 我是 Bill Gurley。我大约在 1997 年来到硅谷，并有幸在 98 年成为一名风险投资人。在我职业生涯的头一整年里，我对跟任何政府部门打交道都毫无兴趣。这对我当时想做的事似乎毫无必要。我是在跟创业者、软件和技术打交道。我看不出这能给我带来什么。直到有一天我遇到了一个问题，我稍后会详细说，这需要

cues.en: me to understand what was going on in Washington. So I checked in with a few advisors. They introduced me to this lawyer in DC. Turns out, DC lawyers do a lot of things that aren't lawyering. And he listened to what he had. He said, I'll call you back. He calls me back. He says, Bill, I got exactly what you need. I found a congressman on the committee that matters to what you're talking about, and I can set up a meeting. I go, great, I'll fly out. He goes, no, no, no, don't fly out. He's coming to you. He goes, he's coming to me? That's pretty nice.
cues.zh: 我去了解华盛顿那边的动向。于是我咨询了几位顾问。他们把我介绍给了华盛顿特区的一位律师。事实证明，华盛顿的律师干的大多数事情都跟法律业务无关。他听完我讲的情况后说：“我回头打给你。”随后他回电说：“Bill，我正好找到了你需要的。我联系到了主管你所说领域的委员会里的一位国会议员，我可以安排一次会面。”我说：“太好了，我飞过去。”他说：“不不不，别飞过来，他去找你。”我想，他来找我？那敢情好。

cues.en: He goes, do you have a conference room? I said, I'm a venture capitalist. We have lots of conference rooms. So he said, I need you to get some people together. And here's the catch. They need to bring $5,000 each. Hung up the phone, started thinking, all right, I got six people. We got board members, CEO, $5,000, $30,000. He's calling me back next week. How's it going? Great, I got six people, $5,000 ready to go. He goes, most of these meetings have 10 to 12 people. He says, shit.
cues.zh: 他问：“你们有会议室吗？”我说：“我是个风投，我们会议室多得是。”于是他说：“我需要你召集一些人，不过有个条件，每人得带 5000 美元来。”挂断电话后，我开始琢磨：行，我能凑齐 6 个人，有董事会成员、CEO，每人 5000，一共 3 万美元。下周他又打来电话问：“进展如何？”“很好，我找了 6 个人，每人 5000，都准备好了。”他说：“这种会一般都有 10 到 12 个人。”我说：“靠。”

cues.en: Like now I'm inviting people that don't even have anything to do with this thing and like having to help them out I'm up 60k. I hang up. He called me back a week later. He goes Bill. How's it going? I got shit. I got 12 people You know, everybody's got a check. We're ready to go. I'm losing interest at this point. He goes Do they have spouses? I'm like, what kind of question is this? Do they have spouses? He goes
cues.zh: 这下我得去请那些根本八竿子打不着的人，还得帮他们垫钱，已经飙到 6 万块了。我挂了电话。一周后他又打过来问：“Bill，进展如何？”我说：“妈的，我找齐 12 个人了，每个人都带了支票，随时可以开始。”此时我已经开始烦了。他却问：“他们有配偶吗？”我心想，这叫什么问题？有配偶吗？他接着说

cues.en: Yeah, let's have their spouses write $5,000 each. I go, our conference room's not big enough for the spouse. He goes, they don't have to come. This is a true story, by the way. True story. And it would go on to happen two more times in my life, and then I stopped meeting with Congressmen. The reason that I needed to engage relates to this company. My fourth VC investment was in a company called Tropos Networks. We had industrial-grade mesh Wi-Fi. You could mount it on a...
cues.zh: “对，让他们配偶每人也开一张 5000 美元的支票。”我说：“我们会议室可坐不下连带配偶这么多人。”他说：“他们人不用来。”顺便说一句，这是个真实的故事。千真万确。这种事后来在我的人生中又发生了两次，之后我就再也不见国会议员了。我之所以需要和他们打交道，是因为这家公司。我的第四笔风投投资了一家名为 Tropos Networks 的公司。我们做的是工业级网状 Wi-Fi。你可以把它安装在……

cues.en: Telephone Poland Bay the city in in Wi-Fi broadband. It was awesome. We are so excited about it We were changing the world. It was disruptive Google got excited about it earth link got excited about it But the customer I loved the most they got excited about were mayors There are hundreds of mayors all over the country that wanted to provide free Wi-Fi service across their downtown area It would help with public safety economic development, of course digital divide
cues.zh: 电线杆上，让整个城市都沉浸在 Wi-Fi 宽带中。太棒了。我们对此极其兴奋，觉得我们正在改变世界。这具有颠覆性，Google 兴奋不已，EarthLink 也很兴奋。但我最喜欢、也最兴奋的客户是市长们。全美有数百位市长希望在他们的市中心区域提供免费 Wi-Fi 服务。这有助于公共安全、经济发展，当然还有消除数字鸿沟。

cues.en: So we were so thrilled. I was so pumped. I was sure we had a winner here. And then one day these two people got excited, which turned out not to be a good thing. This is Mayor Street of Philadelphia and his CIO, Diana Neff. They got just as excited as I did. They were idealistic. They were, you know, optimistic. Maybe they were quixotic. Maybe I was too.
cues.zh: 所以我们激动不已。我热血沸腾，坚信我们胜券在握。然而有一天，这两个人也兴奋起来了，事实证明这可不是件好事。这是费城市长 Street 和他的 CIO Diana Neff。他们跟我一样兴奋。他们充满理想主义，非常乐观，也许还带着点唐吉诃德式的盲目，或许当时的我也一样。

cues.en: Because the next thing that happened is what caused me to get that meeting. You can't read this, but it says, lobbyists try to kill Philly wireless plan. And in the article it says, Philly's plan to offer an inexpensive wireless internet service, the most ambitious yet, collided with commercial interest. Collided with commercial interest. There were no voters or citizens up in arms about this. Commercial interest. How many of you, I know this is a younger crowd, how many of you are old enough to remember Schoolhouse Rock? Awesome.
cues.zh: 因为接下来发生的事，才让我得到了那次会面。你读不到这段，但上面写着：游说者试图扼杀费城无线计划。文章里说，费城要提供廉价无线互联网服务的计划——迄今最有雄心的一个——与商业利益发生了冲突。与商业利益发生了冲突。没有选民或市民为此群情激愤。商业利益。你们有多少人——我知道这是更年轻的人群——有多少人年纪够大，还记得 Schoolhouse Rock？太棒了。

cues.en: So, like you, I learned about how Congress works by ABC Saturday Morning Television. And they told us, there's a phrase in this, I looked up the script, it said some folks back home wanted a law, so they called their local congressman, implying that the people that have the need are the citizens and the people that write the law are the congressman. Imagine how surprised I was when I read this.
cues.zh: 所以，和你们一样，我也是通过 ABC 周六早间电视节目了解国会是如何运作的。他们告诉我们——里面有这么一句话，我查过台词，上面说家乡的某些人想要一项法律，所以他们打电话给当地的国会议员——这意味着提出需求的是公民，而撰写法律的是议员。想象一下，当我读到这篇内容时有多震惊。

cues.en: Philadelphia was embarking on the research phase of the project when Verizon successfully pushed a bill through the state legislature. Verizon's writing legislation? How does that work? Now, it turns out this wasn't even our biggest problem because another company's headquartered in Philadelphia named Comcast. They had put a bill on Governor Rindell's desk, proposal drafted by lobbyists for the telecommunications companies. This isn't what I learned on Schoolhouse Rock.
cues.zh: 费城刚开始进行该项目的调研阶段，Verizon 就成功推动州议会通过了一项法案。Verizon 居然在起草法律？这算怎么回事？事实证明，这甚至还不是我们最大的问题，因为另一家名叫 Comcast 的公司总部也设在费城。他们把一份法案送到了州长 Rendell 的办公桌上，而提案正是电信公司的说客起草的。这可跟我当年在《摇滚校园》里学到的完全不一样。

cues.en: The governor whose bill that was on the desk of is Ed Rendell. He's on the right. Before he was governor, he was mayor of Philadelphia. The gentleman in the middle is named Michael Nutter. He would go on to replace Street and was a longtime council member, but the guy on the left was the real nemesis. This is David Cohen, chief lobbyist for Comcast. Now, David Cohen is to corporate lobbying what Bob Marley is to reggae. He's like...
cues.zh: 法案摆在桌上的那位州长叫 Ed Rendell，他在右边。在当州长之前，他是费城市长。中间的那位叫 Michael Nutter，他后来接替了 Street，此前长期担任市议员。但左边那位才是真正的死对头。这是 David Cohen，Comcast 的首席说客。这么说吧，David Cohen 之于企业游说，就像 Bob Marley 之于雷鬼乐。他就像……

cues.en: There's just there's no there's no second The New York Times did a profile of him called Comcast real repairman in which they say is the most important executive in the whole company and I fundamentally believe that It also says he's probably one of the most savory corporate political operatives in the history of US business The article on the right from the Inquirer calls him Philadelphia's most powerful unelected official
cues.zh: 毫无疑问，绝无仅有。《纽约时报》曾写过一篇关于他的专访，称他为 Comcast 的“真正的修理工”，文中提到他是整个公司最重要的管理高层，我也深以为然。文中还说，他可能是美国商业史上最受赞誉的企业政治操盘手之一。右边《问询报》的这篇文章，则称他是费城“最有权势的非民选官员”。

cues.en: I don't even know how you can put those words together. So here we are. Here we are in our little conference room with our spousal-enhanced checkbooks. And this is like a second-grader challenging Michael Jordan to a game on one-on-one for money. Like, we were pissing in the ocean. We had no chance. No chance. Now guess who offers citywide Wi-Fi? That one's easy.
cues.zh: 我都不知道你怎么能把这些词凑到一块。我们当时就是这个处境。我们就待在自己的小会议室里，手里拿着靠另一半补贴的支票簿。这就像是个二年级小孩为了钱，要和 Michael Jordan 单挑打一场。真的，我们简直就是在沧海一粟。我们毫无胜算。一点机会都没有。现在猜猜谁提供了全城 Wi-Fi？答案显而易见。

cues.en: AT&T would join this fight. Within two years, they would outlaw municipal broadband in over 22 states. They'd just write it into the books and just took the power of these local decision makers away from them, all in the interest of the commercial interest, not the citizen.
cues.zh: AT&T 也加入了这场较量。不到两年，他们就在超过 22 个州促成立法，禁止市政宽带。他们直接把禁令写进法典，剥夺了地方决策者的权力，这一切都只是为了商业利益，而不是为了公民。

cues.en: I wanna talk about another piece of telecom legislation. My partnership back in those days invested in telecom equipment, and so we were very interested in the Telecommunications Act of 1996. This was heralded as the most important telecommunications reform in 62 years. Now this one's simple. I'm just gonna use the headlines from Wikipedia. The Telecommunications Act of 1996 had two goals, to promote competition,
cues.zh: 我想聊聊另一部电信法案。当年我的合伙公司投资过电信设备，所以我们非常关注《1996年电信法案》。它曾被誉为 62 年来最重要的电信改革。这件事其实很简单，我就直接用维基百科上的大纲。《1996年电信法案》有两个目标：促进竞争，

cues.en: and to encourage the rapid development of new technologies. Let's see how things went. In 1996, the top four had 48% markets here. Four, five years later, after this heralded legislation, they're up to 85%. That didn't work. Let's check in on the second one. Were they promoting innovation? This is a chart of VC dollars into telecom equipment.
cues.zh: 以及鼓励新技术的快速发展。我们来看看实际结果如何。1996 年，排名前四的企业占据了 48% 的市场份额。在这部广受赞誉的法案出台四五年后，这一数字飙升到了 85%。促进竞争显然失败了。再来看看第二个目标，它推动创新了吗？这是一张风投资金流向电信设备的图表。

cues.en: This used to be 15% of what VCs did Within 10 years it had gone below 1% and a year later the MVC a stopped tracking it now if you want to talk to one of the expert VCs in Telecommunications equipment, it'll be easy to do because they're retired This market's gone. There is no more innovation in telecom equipment. So what happens here? How can you possibly have?
cues.zh: 这曾经占到风投总额的 15%，不到 10 年就跌破了 1%，一年后 NVCA（美国国家风投协会）干脆不再追踪这项数据了。现在如果你想找电信设备领域的资深风投聊聊，那可太容易了，因为他们都退休了。这个市场已经不复存在，电信设备领域再也没有创新了。怎么会变成这样？怎么可能出现这种情况？

cues.en: a super important bill signed by and implemented by one of the most heralded presidents in our generation that doesn't just fail. Failing would be things stay the same and you don't accomplish the goal. This did even worse. It created the opposite thing of what it was supposed to go do. Let me introduce you to George Stigler. He's the 1982 Nobel Prize winner in economics and the father of regulatory capture.
cues.zh: 一项由我们这一代最负盛名的总统签署并推行的极其重要的法案，不仅失败了——失败无非也就是维持原样、没达到目标——但它的结果甚至更糟，它带来了与初衷完全相反的后果。让我向大家介绍一下 George Stigler。他是 1982 年诺贝尔经济学奖得主，也是“监管俘获”理论的奠基人。

cues.en: This is his most famous quote. As a rule, regulation is acquired by the industry and is designed and operated primarily for its benefit. I'd like to say regulation is the friend of the incumbent. Quick audience interaction moment. That's the one thing I want you to take away. So on the count of three screen, regulation is the friend of the incumbent. One, two, three. Yes! Amen. All right. So.
cues.zh: 这是他最著名的一句名言：“通常而言，监管是由行业争取来的，其设计和运作也主要是为了该行业的利益。”我喜欢把它总结为：监管是在位者的朋友。来个简短的现场互动，这是我希望大家今天能带走的核心观点。我数到三，大家一起喊：“监管是在位者的朋友！”一、二、三。太棒了！完全没错。好的。

cues.en: This is the only slide I have with bullets because this is gonna be a two-minute regulatory capture 101, all from George Stigler's notes. The first thing he says, in regulatory capture, a special interest is prioritized over the general interest of the public. Sound familiar from my other stories? Leading to a net loss for society, a net loss for society, that's important. The two mechanisms they usually use is the second bullet.
cues.zh: 这是我唯一带项目符号的 PPT，因为接下来是两分钟的“监管俘获入门课”，全都来自 George Stigler 的理论笔记。他指出的第一点是：在监管俘获中，特定群体的特殊利益被置于公众普遍利益之上。听着是不是和刚才讲的故事很像？这会导致社会的净损失，请记住，是对社会的净损失。而第二点，则是他们通常使用的两种手段。

cues.en: limited market entry, and price protection, or even price increases, which I'll show you more of. And then the mechanisms of influence are money made worse by Citizens United, exposure, just time around people, and then three revolving doors. This is super important, and I'll show you one great example of that. That's people moving in and out. When they interviewed Christie on the pod the other day, they were talking about this in the military. All right.
cues.zh: 限制市场准入、价格保护，甚至涨价，这些我后面会多讲。然后是影响机制：金钱——被 Citizens United 弄得更糟——曝光度，也就是跟人相处的时间，还有三种旋转门。这非常重要，我会给你们看一个很好的例子。也就是人进人出。前几天他们在播客里采访 Christie 时，就谈到了军队里的这种情况。好。

cues.en: This is a piece of Morgan Stanley research from 1999. Someone took the time to go study five pieces of major US legislation that had happened over the years and how the incumbent stocks did after the legislation. And let's just steal a few sentences from this. Conclude that landmark regulatory action is a tendency to improve returns for the largest players in the targeted industry.
cues.zh: 这是 Morgan Stanley 1999 年的一份研究。有人花时间研究了美国多年来发生的五项重大立法，以及立法后现有企业的股票表现。我们从中摘几句话。结论是，重大监管行动往往会提高目标行业中最大参与者的回报。

cues.en: Long-term investors should consider capitalizing on any temporary weakness caused by market reaction to regulation. Many attempts to increase competition or improve customer experience have failed. This is reinforcing what Stigler taught us. Here's a very simple quick one. Number of new banks in the US, 2009, nothing. Dodd-Frank. Like, that's what happens. All right, two really good stories. You might not even believe them, because they're so outlandish.
cues.zh: 长期投资者应考虑利用市场对监管反应所造成的任何暂时疲软。许多增加竞争或改善客户体验的尝试都失败了。这再次印证了 Stigler 教给我们的东西。这里有个非常简单的例子。美国新银行数量，2009 年，零。Dodd-Frank。就是这样。好，接下来两个非常好的故事。你可能都不信，因为它们太离谱了。

cues.en: Does everyone know who epic is? It's hard to know because they're not public. It's a very large private company in Wisconsin That is the largest player in medical EHR software medical records, and this is their CEO Judith Faulkner now in Get the year right 2009 Obama put her on his health IT counsel. She was the only corporate representative Should not surprise you
cues.zh: 大家都知道 Epic 是谁吗？很难知道，因为他们没上市。它是威斯康星州一家非常大的私营公司，是医疗 EHR 软件、病历领域的最大玩家。这是他们的 CEO Judith Faulkner。年份没错，2009 年，Obama 把她放进了他的卫生 IT 委员会。她是唯一的企业代表。这应该不会让你意外

cues.en: that she's a major donor to Obama. Now, Obama passed the American Recovery Act. That was his big piece of stimulus, kind of like Biden's inflation act that happened recently. And tucked underneath that, easy to hide in this big bill, is an act that was the acronym's high tech. It's this health information technology thing. And then they created an agency called ONC that oversaw it. Now, this is the part you're not going to believe. They came up with a brilliant idea.
cues.zh: 她是 Obama 的重要捐赠者。后来，Obama 通过了 American Recovery Act。那是他的大规模刺激法案，有点像 Biden 最近搞的通胀法案。而藏在那下面——很容易藏在这项大法案里——是一项缩写为 HITECH 的法案。就是那个卫生信息技术的东西。然后他们成立了一个叫 ONC 的机构来监管它。接下来这部分你可能不会信。他们想出了一个绝妙的主意。

cues.en: I have to assume she helped encourage this. Doctors would receive $44,000 each if they bought software. $38 billion. This is true, you can look it up. I'm not making it up. $44,000, give it to a doctor, implement some software. Many of you run companies, that'd be pretty cool, right? The government passed a law, say, buy your software, they get money. Make it a lot easier. Now, you may be thinking,
cues.zh: 我只能假设她帮忙推动了这件事。医生只要买软件，每人就能拿到 44,000 美元。380 亿美元。这是真的，你可以去查。我没编。44,000 美元，给一个医生，装点软件。你们很多人经营公司，这挺酷的吧？政府通过法律，说买你的软件，他们就能拿钱。这下容易多了。现在，你可能在想，

cues.en: Are doctors needy? But here's the catch. Remember, this happened because of the mortgage meltdown. Doctors own multiple homes, so they have multiple mortgages. They probably needed the assistant. Now, there's two more things about this act. They're also unbelievable. First, there's a flaw. If someone said, I'm going to pay people to buy software, most people would be like, well, you're going to have a problem. They're going to buy it, and they're not going to use it. Well, they thought of that. So guess what?
cues.zh: 医生很缺钱吗？但问题来了。记住，这事发生是因为房贷崩盘。医生拥有多套房，所以有多笔房贷。他们可能确实需要这笔补助。关于这个法案还有两件事。也同样难以置信。首先，有个缺陷。如果有人说，我要付钱让人买软件，大多数人会说，那你会有个问题：他们会买，但不会用。结果他们想到了这一点。所以你猜怎么着？

cues.en: The second phase, doctors got paid 17,000 more dollars to prove they were using it. This is called meaningful use. Plastered all over the website of all the HR vendors at the time. It gets even better. So the ONC decided the threshold of features you would need for your software to comply with this mandate.
cues.zh: 到了第二阶段，医生只要证明自己在用它，就能再拿17000美元。这叫“有效使用”。当时所有电子病历厂商的官网上都贴满了这个词。更绝的还在后头。ONC（国家卫生信息技术协调办公室）划定了一套功能门槛，你的软件必须满足这些功能才算合规。

cues.en: I'm assuming they kind of took Epic's feature set and plowed it into this spreadsheet.
